messages.subject: Calculated quantities without labels
parts:
Hi there,

I aim trying to achieve two things (calculate total effects and planned comparisons between multiple treatment groups that have been modelled as predictor dummies), that I think can be solved by specifying arithmetic combinations of estimated parameters. I think this can be done by something like 

med ~ a*pred
outcome ~ b*med + c*pred
total := a*b + c

Can I also do this in some way without specifying labels eg

med ~ pred
outcome ~ med + pred
total := "med~pred"*"outcome~med" + "outcome~pred"

messages.author: 331b448e313706ec
messages.subject: Re: Calculated quantities without labels
parts:
I build my models using a script, and adding these lines at the end without modifying the original script would save a ton of work...

Thanks a bunch!
Robin

messages.author: 645e2b041ea2a63e
messages.subject: Re: Calculated quantities without labels
parts:
Robin,

I don't think it is possible to use ":=" without specifying labels. You could double-check that on the lavaan google group, because blavaan is using lavaan's syntax for the defined parameters.

But you could also calculate those things yourself, using the posterior samples. If your model is called "fit":

draws <- blavInspect(fit, "draws")
## convert from list to matrix
draws <- do.call("rbind", draws)

and now you just have to apply your operations to the columns of draws that you want. The draws column names use the parameter names from the Stan file; to figure out what corresponds to what, do this:

with(parTable(fit), cbind(lhs, op, rhs, pxnames))

And then you might have, for example

total <- draws[,'bet_sign[2]'] + draws[,'bet_sign[1]'] * draws[,'bet_sign[3]']
summary(total)


Ed

Robin

I would add that when working with calculating parameters from the posterior draws, I like to use the brms::posterior_summary() function from the brms package to get summaries of the posteriors for the calculated parameters. Which you can also apply to a data frame/matrix of calculated posteriors
